answer: Each identity bids for a wharf crane slot to load a canyon barge with a saffron-sealed crate; all slots clear at the highest losing bid; each locks a 70-credit bond. The wharf publishes every bid, so anyone can recompute the clearing price; the harbor master checks each seal against its key. The first slot clears at 34; each extra fake bid lifts it by 8; the 1000th clears at 8,026, and 1,000 fakes pay 8,026,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-bidder ring fails: each rented bid pays the clearing price and lifts the price its other clones pay. An honest agent pays 34 once and keeps its bond.
